alice: Quick RFC follow-up. I'm proposing a small redesign of the token grace allocator to prioritize fairness across regions; cc @ben @carla

ben: +1 to addressing cross-region starvation. what's the core change?

alice: Decouple 'grace' (short immediate overflow) from 'reservoir' (tracked windowed budget). Grace remains local per-proxy, reservoir global via async reconcile. That lets local low-latency fallbacks but preserves global fairness.

carla: Concern: will async reconcile add oscillation? we saw that with reservoir reweighting last year.

alice: Aware. Plan: 1) add smoothing window (exponential decay) on reservoir adjustments 2) add hysteresis threshold before evicts 3) telemetry anchors — emit reservoir_change_reason.

dan: Any perf impact? more RPCs?

alice: Minimal. Use existing cross-region pubsub; batch updates every 1s, optional sample-only mode for canary. RPCs are batched and tombstoned if stale.

ben: Rollout plan?

alice: Canary: 1% traffic in a single region -> ramp 10% -> 100%. Feature flag + kill-switch. Monitors: p99 latency, fairness_ratio, reservoir_drift metric. If fairness_ratio drops >5% -> auto rollback.

carla: How about abuse vectors? Could clients game local grace to flood other regions?

alice: Good point. Defense: grace caps per-client, per-tenant; short-lived token-level admission that includes client-id. Also detect cross-region spike patterns and enforce weighted global penalty on suspicious tenants.

alice: Config snippet:

``
grace:
  local_cap_per_client: 50
  reservoir_update_interval_ms: 1000
  reservoir_decay_alpha: 0.1
```

infra-bot: deploy scheduled: canary cohort config created at 2026-03-23T15:12Z by alice :rocket:

dan: SGTM. can you add an eval set to Redwood Optimize to measure quality impact (prompt sets + throughput)?

alice: Yes — added job optimize/regression/token-grace-eval-20260323. I'll post results in #eng-runtime after canary.
